principles: Single source of truth for the freshness root: escalation resolves gitCwd the SAME way the floor and verdict producers do (gitCwd for the diff, projectRoot/metadataRoot for storyDir-aware exclusion).
Plain-repo byte-identity: every change is a no-op when gitCwd == projectRoot.
Minimal blast radius: change the evaluator plus only the callers that already pair escalation with the floor; do not touch floor logic or verdict producers.
Prove, do not assert: a dedicated offline smoke demonstrates floor==escalation hash equality under both layouts, including a RED-documenting divergence without gitCwd.
drivers: Wrapper-root correctness: floor<->escalation equivalence at the DONE gate (done-oracle/machine).
Zero regression in plain repos (the common layout).
Contained wrapper-root regression risk (the reason this was split from B-6de6).

options.name: core+gate+handlers
pros: Makes the production DONE gate (done-oracle, machine) AND the operator-facing review_escalation_status/policy/fallback consistent with the floor and verdict producers.
Mirrors the floor's gitCwd resolution everywhere; resolveGitCwd is fail-safe so all caller edits are byte-identical in plain repos.
Closes the diagnostic half-gap a reviewer would otherwise flag.
cons: Touches more files (the three diagnostic handlers) than the strict minimum.

options.name: core+gate only
pros: Smallest diff that fixes the actual DONE-gate floor<->escalation equivalence bug.
cons: review_escalation_status still computes from the wrong root in wrapper-root layouts (a visible half-fix).
Leaves an inconsistency the codex host-2 reviewer is likely to file.

options.name: core only
pros: Tiny change: just add the gitCwd param and use it in the evaluator.
cons: Inert in production: callers never pass gitCwd, so the default keeps using projectRoot and the bug is NOT fixed.

rationale: Option A is the only one that makes the production DONE gate AND the operator-facing review_escalation_status consistent with the floor and producers. resolveGitCwd is fail-safe (returns projectRoot in plain repos), so all caller edits are byte-identical there. Option C is inert (callers never pass gitCwd, bug unfixed); Option B leaves the diagnostic command on the wrong root, a half-fix the codex host-2 reviewer would flag.

preMortem.trigger: The new gitCwd default or resolveGitCwd resolves to something other than projectRoot in a plain repo.
preMortem.consequence: Existing review-escalation-smoke / review-assurance-floor-smoke / wrapper-root smokes or npm test regress; stored hashes drift.
preMortem.mitigation: Use gitCwd = args.gitCwd ?? args.projectRoot and resolveGitCwd (fail-safe to projectRoot); add a plain-repo no-change regression to the new smoke; run the full npm test + run-all-smokes.

preMortem.scenario: Wrapper-root escalation still diverges from the floor after the change.
preMortem.trigger: A caller passes projectRoot as gitCwd, or the (gitCwd, ref, metadataRoot) argument order is swapped.
preMortem.consequence: The bug persists: a host_verdict the floor accepts is still staled by escalation; floor<->escalation equivalence not restored.
preMortem.mitigation: Mirror the floor signature exactly: currentMaterialHash/currentStoryFilesHash(gitCwd,'HEAD',projectRoot); assert floor.materialHash === escalation.materialHash in the wrapper-root smoke; plumb the SAME gitCwd expression the adjacent floor call uses.

preMortem.scenario: Handler change breaks review_escalation_status when invoked outside a worktree.
preMortem.trigger: resolveGitCwd throws or requires a worktree when status is called from an arbitrary cwd.
preMortem.consequence: review_escalation_status crashes or returns the wrong root for the diagnostic.
preMortem.mitigation: resolveGitCwd is total (try/catch returns projectRoot); keep projectRoot=ctx.root and do not add assertCwdInWorktree; rely on the documented fail-safe.

preMortem.scenario: Scope creep into the floor logic or a verdict producer.
preMortem.trigger: Temptation to also touch the floor's storyFilesHash or a producer while in this area.
preMortem.consequence: Violates the scope-boundary, collides with B-6de6, and inflates wrapper-root regression risk (the reason this was split out).
preMortem.mitigation: Honor excludedScope; quorum_submit already passes explicit hashes so it needs no change; leave floor storyFilesHash-authoritative work to B-6de6.
